ThinkByte: Mukul M, Harsha Thota, Samarpith Rout, Charan Kumar, Pavan Kalyan
Sigmainfo: to: Shiresha Madhury
Key Takeaways

Subtopics and search intent details have been structured for the content blocks; primary, secondary, semantic, and long-tail keywords must be integrated into upcoming landing pages without altering the approved Fintech document.
Duplicate content issues were raised regarding the Fintech pages, with a directive to use 301 redirects for Indian versions to avoid internal competition and streamline SEO.
The blog repository is to reflect a mixed bag of verticals with a target of 15 blocks per month, drawing from detailed published counts and ensuring interlinking across content to drive leads.

The keyword research for key verticals—especially product engineering services, Fintech, business intelligence, and AI—must be completed by Friday to support the blog repository and landing page improvements.
A follow-up meeting is tentatively scheduled for Friday around 12:30 to review finalized keywords and the block calendar, ensuring timely rollout for the next publishing cycle.

Keyword Audit and Research for Landing Pages
Emphasis on incorporating primary, secondary, semantic, and long tail keywords for subtopics such as cloud native and microservices, modeled on prior financial services research.
Keywords will be sourced using Google API, Keyword Planner, and Semrush, with a repository exceeding 5,000 keywords, ensuring comprehensive coverage.
Deadline targets were discussed, with the expectation to complete keyword research for 33 subpages by Friday, ensuring the content for premier verticals is ready.
Blog Repository and Block Calendar Planning
The internal blog repository spans from April to August with specific publication counts: May with 8 blocks, June with 9 blocks, July with 12 blocks, and August aiming for 16-17 blocks.
The blogs are strategically intended to support landing pages, with at least two blog interlinking opportunities per published block.
A block calendar of 15 mixed-content blogs for the next month was proposed, covering verticals such as fintech, product engineering services, and business intelligence.
International SEO and Duplicate Page Issues
Concerns were raised regarding duplicate content between the US-focused fintech pages and previous Indian traffic pages, which have only slight keyword differences.
A solution proposed was the use of 301 redirects to consolidate pages, thereby favoring the US audience while de-prioritizing Indian leads.

Additional website audit findings include issues with duplicate titles and descriptions, pagination errors, missing alt texts, and a broken link, all to be consolidated into one document for the web team.
Timeline and Deadlines for Content Finalization
Fintech blog topics and keyword suggestions are expected to finalize by Tuesday EOD, whereas broader keyword research for other verticals should be prepared by Thursday morning.

A clear deadline was set for completing the keyword audit for key verticals (product engineering, business intelligence, AI/ML) by Friday, with the updated list needed for a Friday meeting with Sandeep.
Early content planning is crucial as the first blog for landing pages is scheduled to go live on September 1, aligning with the internal publication schedule.
Blog Publication Schedule and Vertical Prioritization
Emphasis was placed on a mixed-content strategy, ensuring that the upcoming block calendar includes blog posts from fintech, product engineering, business intelligence, and other verticals.

Prioritization guidelines suggest focusing on higher-volume verticals (e.g., fintech and product engineering) by assigning more block topics to these areas, while leaving some spots open for lower priority services.
The meeting confirmed a publishing schedule of three blogs per week on Monday, Wednesday, and Thursday, with flexibility to produce additional blogs if delays occur.
Follow-up Meeting
Team members were reminded not to directly edit the fintech content document but to add comments instead, preserving the integrity of approved content.
Instructions were given to ensure the consolidation of website audit findings into one document for easier tracking with the web development team.
Plan to catch up on Friday for status update around keyword research and block calendar.
A follow-up meeting was proposed for Friday at 12:30 PM to review the progress on keyword research and block calendar planning, with confirmation communicated via WhatsApp.
Tentative meeting time on Friday around 12:00 or 12:30 was suggested.
